This page documents a [[id:31C868B9-306E-4282-BA8C-07E647021B34][task]] in the [[id:BC5582FB-1648-42F2-9D6A-B6DB6EEBC676][Acme Corporation follow-ups: manual chapter, logo fixes, synthetic feeds]] story. It captures the goal, current status, acceptance, and any notes or results.

* Goal

GLEIF counterparty import should have first-class support for
attaching a logo/flag image to a counterparty when one is available,
instead of the demo-only bolt-on this replaces.

The removed code (=tenant_handler.hpp::attach_demo_counterparty_logo=,
called from =provision_acme= after Step 7) polled
=get_counterparties_request= every 2 seconds for up to 8 minutes
waiting for the GLEIF import (Step 2, ~13k rows, by far the largest
and slowest bundle publish in the whole flow) to land BARCLAYS PLC,
then copied a hardcoded =demo_counterparty_logo= template image onto
it. Problems with that approach:

- It's a random, disconnected extra step tacked onto the *end* of
  =provision_acme=, unrelated to the GLEIF import that actually
  produces the counterparty rows it depends on.
- The up-to-8-minute silent poll (only failures log anything) reads
  exactly like a hang from the caller's side — this cost significant
  debugging time working out it wasn't actually stuck, just slow.
- It's hardcoded to one specific counterparty (BARCLAYS PLC) for demo
  purposes, not a general mechanism.

The fix belongs in the GLEIF import/publish pipeline itself: when a
GLEIF counterparty entity has a known logo (LEI-keyed or similar),
attach it as part of that same publish, not as a separate polling
step racing the import's own completion.

* Acceptance

- GLEIF counterparty publish attaches a logo image to a counterparty
  when one is available, as part of that same publish pipeline (no
  separate post-hoc polling step in =provision_acme= or elsewhere).
- BARCLAYS PLC (or whichever counterparty is used to demonstrate this)
  ends up with a rendering logo after a normal =--source acme=
  provisioning run, with no unbounded/silent wait.
- =attach_demo_counterparty_logo= and its call site in
  =tenant_handler.hpp= (already removed as part of this discovery) stay
  removed; the replacement lives in the GLEIF/refdata layer.

* Plan

=attach_demo_counterparty_logo= and its call site were already removed
from =tenant_handler.hpp= before this task started (see the task's own
description) -- the remaining work was adding the replacement, not
removing the old code.

Implemented directly in
=ores_refdata_publish_lei_counterparties_from_dq_fn= (in
=refdata_publish_from_dq_create.sql=), the same SQL function that
inserts the GLEIF counterparty rows themselves -- part of the one
publish, not a second pass:

- A small, extensible =(lei, image_key)= VALUES list of known logos.
  One entry today: Barclays Plc's real LEI
  (=213800LBQA1Y9L22JB70=) -> the =demo_counterparty_logo= template
  key. LEI chosen over =short_code= as the join key since LEIs are
  the dataset's own stable identifier -- short codes are generated
  per-import (=ores_utility_generate_short_code_fn=) and can
  theoretically collide/renumber, LEIs never do.
- Each tenant gets its own copy of the system-tenant template image
  (via =ores_assets_get_template_image_fn=, the existing
  cross-tenant-isolation reader), created once per tenant and reused
  on subsequent publishes into the same tenant (looked up first by
  =(tenant_id, key)= before copying) -- mirrors how the old C++
  =copy_template_image= worked, just done in SQL now.
- After the per-depth-level counterparty insert loop, one small
  block loops the logo map, skips LEIs not present in this import's
  =lei_counterparty_uuid_map= temp table, resolves/copies the
  per-tenant image, and =UPDATE=s the matching counterparty's
  =image_id=.

No unbounded/silent wait: the whole thing runs inline in the same
transaction as the counterparty insert, so a counterparty with a
known LEI has its logo the instant the import completes -- nothing
racing GLEIF's own ~13k-row import in a separate polling loop.

* Result

Implemented in =ores_refdata_publish_lei_counterparties_from_dq_fn=
(=refdata_publish_from_dq_create.sql=) -- see =* Plan= for the full
mechanism. Verified end-to-end against a fresh =--source acme=
provisioning run: BARCLAYS PLC (short_code =BRCLYS=) has =image_id=
set immediately after the GLEIF publish completes, with no separate
polling step. Manual scenario [[id:07E8D2EB-3D73-4216-8FE1-9EC04EDC8D4E][Verify GLEIF import attaches counterparty
logo natively]] (PASSED, 4/4 steps): the logo renders in
=CounterpartyDetailDialog= (confirming this fix together with the
earlier logo-rendering fix in this story), and no other counterparty
picked up a logo -- the known-logo map stays scoped to Barclays' LEI.

Side finding during manual verification, filed separately rather than
fixed here: the Counterparties list has no search, making it hard to
locate a specific record among ~13k GLEIF-imported rows -- [[id:B3FD623C-D87B-491F-9FA2-08B26D67114F][Add
server-side search/filter to list windows across entities]].

Local build clean (linux-clang-debug-make); ctest 71/71 passed.
